assertions.note: General pattern in weak-tie theory; not every weak tie bridges distinct groups.
Homophily is dimension- and context-specific; similarity does not imply a tie in every case.
Benefits of brokerage depend on organizational and network context.
Centrality is not a single property; measures capture distinct structural intuitions.
Observed network association may reflect selection, influence, common causes, or measurement processes.

provenance.method: Atomic claims synthesized conservatively from scholarly textbooks, reviews, methods references and foundational articles. Theory-laden constructs are marked through theory_dependence valuations and notes.

warnings: This corpus describes social structures and interactions; it is not a normative guide to how societies should be organized.
Individual, group and institution are analytical levels, not a causal hierarchy.
Network association does not by itself establish social influence or causality.
Constructs such as institutional isomorphism, social capital and structural holes are theory-dependent and are labelled accordingly.
